title: Aircraft Components Repair Supervisor (Acft Comp Repair Supv)
raw_text:
10-15K. MOS 15K--Aircraft Components Repair Supervisor (Acft Comp Repair Supv), CMF 15
     a. Major duties. The aircraft component repair supervisor must be knowledgeable of the duties
performed by personnel in MOSs 15B, 15D, 15G, and 15H. Performs administrative duties such as
planning aircraft maintenance areas, component and avionics repair shops/facilities as well as
determining man-hours, personnel management, parts and facility requirements while maintaining supply
economy and discipline. Prepares evaluations, special reports, records and recommends and/or
administers plans and policies pertaining to aircraft component repair. Instructs and supervises
maintenance, repairs and inspections of aircraft components and other systems according to drawings,
blueprints, directives, technical manuals, and safety procedures. Typically assigned to Aviation Field or
Sustainment maintenance units.
     b. Physical demands rating and qualifications for initial award of MOS.
       (1) Aircraft component repair supervisors must possess the following qualifications: Waivers,
ACASP qualification, and/or exceptions must be approved by Cdr, AVCOE, ATTN: ATZQ-CDF-P, Ft
Rucker, AL 36362-1100, (https://home.army.mil/rucker/about/AVCOE/opfd/enlisted)
           (a) A physical demands rating Moderate (Gold).
           (b) A physical profile of 323222.
           (c) Normal color vision.
           (d) Qualifying scores - Line scores are the same as the feeder MOS. A Minimum OPAT score of
Standing Long Jump (LJ) -0120 cm, Seated Power Throw (PT) - 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) - 0120
lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) - 0036 shuttles in Physical Demands Category “Moderate” (Gold).
           (e) Formal training (completion of a resident MOS 15B, 15D, 15G, or 15H course conducted
under the auspices of AVCOE) is mandatory.
           (f) Reclassification: Must meet the above qualifications and all prerequisites IAW AR 614-200
“Reclassification of primary military occupational specialty and/or secondary military occupational
specialty” chapter and AR 40-501 “Medical Fitness Standards for Retention and Separation, including
Retirement” chapter. Aircraft Component Repair Supervisor must have an aviation
maintenance/component repairer CMF 15 MOS for a minimum of 18 months at skill level 3.
               1. Active Component: Soldiers that do not meet the above qualifications must submit a
determination packet to Cdr, AVCOE, ATTN: ATZQ-CDF-P, Ft Rucker, AL 36362-1100,
(https://home.army.mil/rucker/about/AVCOE/opfd/enlisted).
               2. National Guard: Soldiers that do not meet the above qualifications must submit a
determination packet through National Guard Bureau, ATTN: NGB-ARNG-AV, 111 South George Mason
Drive, Arlington, VA 22204-1382 (ng.ncr.ngb-arng.mbx.avn-trng mgt@army.mil).
               3. Reserve Component: Soldiers that do not meet the above qualifications must submit a
determination packet through Commander, Army Reserve Aviation Command (ARAC), ATTN: G3 (AFAK-
OPT), 1160 Brandenburg Station Road, Ft Knox, KY 40121-4190, (usarmy.usarc.arac.list.g-37-
training@army.mil).
       (2) MOS closed for reclassification to Soldiers who have been deemed permanently non-deployable
in accordance with AR 40-501, AR 220-1, AR 600-8-101, and AR 614-30. Soldiers must meet the
minimum criteria for retainability stated in AR 635-40, paragraph 3-5(a) and be fully deployable to all
locations and echelons.
     c. Additional skill identifiers. (Note: Refer to table 12-8 (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all
enlisted MOS)).
     d. Physical requirements and standards of grade. Physical requirements and SG relating to each skill
level are listed in the following tables:
       (1) Table 10-15K-1. Physical requirements.
       (2) Table 10-15K-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
       (3) Table 10-15K-3. Standards of grade TDA.

Aircraft Components Repair Supervisor (Acft Comp Repair Supv), CMF 15 a.
Supervise the maintenance or repair of transportation systems or system components.
The aircraft component repair supervisor must be knowledgeable of the duties performed by personnel in MOSs 15B, 15D, 15G, and 15H.

Maintain, repair, and rebuild aircraft structures, functional components, and parts, such as wings and fuselage, rigging, hydraulic units, oxygen systems, fuel systems, electrical systems, gaskets, or seals.

Performs administrative duties such as planning aircraft maintenance areas, component and avionics repair shops/facilities as well as determining man-hours, personnel management, parts and facility requirements while maintaining supply economy and discipline.
Review damage reports, prepare or review repair cost estimates, and plan work to be performed.
Prepares evaluations, special reports, records and recommends and/or administers plans and policies pertaining to aircraft component repair.
Inspect work of aircraft mechanics performing maintenance, modification, or repair and overhaul of aircraft and aircraft mechanical systems to ensure adherence to standards and procedures.
Instructs and supervises maintenance, repairs and inspections of aircraft components and other systems according to drawings, blueprints, directives, technical manuals, and safety procedures.
Coordinate work with that of engineers, technicians, and other aircraft maintenance personnel.
Typically assigned to Aviation Field or Sustainment maintenance units.
Contact supervisors or offices to receive repair assignments.

(1) Aircraft component repair supervisors must possess the following qualifications: Waivers, ACASP qualification, and/or exceptions must be approved by Cdr, AVCOE, ATTN: ATZQ-CDF-P, Ft Rucker, AL 36362-1100, (https://home.army.mil/rucker/about/AVCOE/opfd/enlisted) (a) A physical demands rating Moderate (Gold).
Coordinate work with that of engineers, technicians, and other aircraft maintenance personnel.
Aircraft Component Repair Supervisor must have an aviation maintenance/component repairer CMF 15 MOS for a minimum of 18 months at skill level 3.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
